standard_prerequisites.name: Mere proposition
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type is a mere proposition when any two of its elements are equal.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on both sides.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-inverse criterion
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is an equivalence as soon as it has a two-sided inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is how the equivalence is produced from the two implications.

core_obligations: Given implications in both directions, form the composite in each order (source lines 298-298).
Show each composite is the identity by observing that its two values lie in a mere proposition, so that the required equality holds without further work (source lines 299-300).
Conclude that the two implications are quasi-inverses and hence that the types are equivalent (source lines 300-301).

proof_roadmap.step: Form the two composites from the given implications.
Each composite is the identity because both sides lie in a mere proposition.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 294-296 (book Lemma 3.3.3): two mere propositions that imply each other are equivalent. The statement is a logical equivalence between types and the proof (source lines 297-301) has to turn the two implications into a two-sided inverse, which requires proving that each composite is the identity function; that step is not formal, it uses the hypothesis that both types are mere propositions so that the two values of each composite are equal by propositionality rather than by computation. Which hypothesis does the work, and where, is invisible in the statement.
